# World Monitor [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja-JP.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md) **Real-time global intelligence dashboard** — AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface. The World Monitor name and wordmark identify the official site at [www.worldmonitor.app](https://www.worldmonitor.app), so please don't present a fork as the official site.

         

       

     

Documentation  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

## Ways to Use It | Surface | Get it | Docs | |---------|--------|------| | **Web app** | [worldmonitor.app](https://www.worldmonitor.app) and the tech, finance, commodity, happy and energy variants | [Getting Started](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started) | | **Desktop app** (Tauri) | Windows, macOS and Linux downloads above | [Desktop App](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/desktop-app) | | **Terminal dashboard** | `npx worldmonitor` | [Terminal Dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard) | | **CLI** | `npm install -g worldmonitor` or `brew install worldmonitor` | [Command-Line Client](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli) | | **SDKs** | Python `worldmonitor-sdk`, Ruby `worldmonitor`, Go `sdk/go` | [SDKs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks) | | **MCP server** | `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` | [MCP Overview](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/mcp-overview) | The terminal dashboard runs the same live data in your shell: world map, news, markets, conflict, military flights, cyber, climate, prediction markets and live TV, with mouse support and colour themes. No API key needed. --- ## What It Does - **Curated news feeds** across global and regional categories, AI-synthesized into briefs - **Dual map engine** — 3D globe (globe.gl) and WebGL flat map (deck.gl) with a shared map-layer catalog - **Panel inventory** — concrete panel implementations across specialized variants - **Cross-stream correlation** — military, economic, disaster, and escalation signal convergence - **[Country Instability Index (CII)](https://www.worldmonitor.app/country-instability-index/)** — live CII v14 scores, bands, and approximate 24-hour movement for 31 Tier-1 countries - **Finance radar** — stock exchanges, commodities, crypto, and a market composite - **Local AI** — run everything with Ollama, no API keys required - **Site variants** from a single codebase (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy) - **Native desktop app** (Tauri 2) for macOS, Windows, and Linux - **Multilingual UI** with native-language feeds and RTL support For the full feature list, architecture, data sources, and algorithms, see the **[documentation](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/documentation)**. --- ## Support Status All site variants and desktop binaries are built from a single codebase and ship from the same release process. The table below clarifies maintenance status so you know which surfaces are safe to depend on. | Surface | Status | Notes | |---------|--------|-------| | `worldmonitor.app`, `tech.`, `finance.`, `commodity.`, `happy.`, `energy.` | Stable | Public deployments built from this repo, actively maintained | | Desktop binaries (Windows / macOS Apple Silicon / macOS Intel / Linux AppImage x64 and ARM64) | Stable | One Tauri binary for every variant — install World Monitor and switch to tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy in-app. There is deliberately no per-variant download | | `worldmonitor` npm package (terminal dashboard and CLI) | Stable | Published from [`cli/`](cli/) on every `cli-v*` tag | Issues filed against any of the above are triaged from the same backlog — see the [issues board](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/issues) for currently-open work. --- ## Quick Start **One-line install** (self-host the full stack with Docker — dashboard, Redis, AIS relay, seeded public data): ```bash curl -fsSL https://www.worldmonitor.app/install.sh | bash ``` This clones into `./worldmonitor` (or reuses your checkout), generates the required secrets, starts the stack, and seeds data. Then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Options: `--dir`, `--port`, `--no-seed`, `--no-build`, passed after `bash -s --` (see `scripts/install.sh --help`). API keys are optional. Details, production notes, and uninstall: [SELF_HOSTING.md](./SELF_HOSTING.md). **Local development** (hot-reload Vite server): Requires Node.js 24, the version pinned in `.nvmrc`. Distribution packages are often older. Debian 12 and Raspberry Pi OS ship Node.js 18 with npm 9.2.0, where `npm install` stops with `Invalid comparator: file:vendor/braces`. Install Node.js 24 with [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm) (`nvm install` inside the checkout reads `.nvmrc`) or from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download). ```bash git clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git cd worldmonitor npm install npm run dev ``` Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (override the port with `DEV_PORT` in `.env.local`). The app runs with no environment variables. Feature-specific data sources may require credentials. See `.env.example` for the full list. For variant-specific development: ```bash npm run dev:tech # tech.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:finance # finance.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:commodity # commodity.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:happy # happy.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:energy # energy.worldmonitor.app ``` See the **[self-hosting guide](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started)** for deployment options (Vercel, Docker, static). --- ## Tech Stack | Category | Technologies | |----------|-------------| | **Frontend** | Vanilla TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL | | **Desktop** | Tauri 2 (Rust) with Node.js sidecar | | **AI/ML** | Ollama / OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side) | | **API Contracts** | Protocol Buffers and sebuf HTTP annotations | | **Deployment** | Vercel Edge Functions, Railway relay, Tauri, PWA | | **Caching** | Redis (Upstash), 3-tier cache, CDN, service worker | Full stack details in the **[architecture docs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/architecture)**. --- ## Programmatic Access World Monitor is built for agents and scripts as well as browsers: - **MCP server** — `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Public `tools/list`; `tools/call` authenticates with a `X-WorldMonitor-Key` header or OAuth. The server also publishes its Agent Skills through the draft `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension (`skills/list`, `skills/get`, and `skill://…` resource reads). - **Google Antigravity and Gemini listing preparation** — install the bundled Antigravity plugin (`.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` + `mcp_config.json`) with `agy plugin install ./worldmonitor`. Gemini custom apps and Connected Apps sign in through Google's OAuth callbacks. See [Gemini and Antigravity](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/gemini-antigravity). - **REST API** — base `https://api.worldmonitor.app`, described by the [OpenAPI spec](https://worldmonitor.app/openapi.yaml). - **CLI** — the official [`worldmonitor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) npm package (source in [`cli/`](cli/)). Run it with no arguments in a terminal for the [terminal dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard): ```sh npx worldmonitor tools # run ad-hoc — list every MCP tool (no key needed) npm install -g worldmonitor # or install the `worldmonitor` (alias `wm`) command brew install worldmonitor # or install it with Homebrew worldmonitor risk IR --api-key wm_xxx ``` - **SDKs** — official zero-dependency client libraries mirroring the CLI: Python [`worldmonitor-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/worldmonitor-sdk/) (source in [`sdk/python/`](sdk/python/)), Ruby [`worldmonitor`](https://rubygems.org/gems/worldmonitor) ([`sdk/ruby/`](sdk/ruby/)), Go [`github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go) ([`sdk/go/`](sdk/go/)). Guide: [worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks). aiSummary.oneLiner: A real-time global intelligence dashboard utilizing AI and dual map engines to track geopolitical and infrastructure...
aiSummary.whatItDoes: World Monitor serves as a comprehensive situational awareness platform that aggregates over 500 curated news feeds, synthesizing them into actionable briefs via local AI models like Ollama without requiring external API keys. It employs a dual map engine utilizing both globe.gl and deck.gl to visualize 56 distinct layers of military, economic, and disaster data. The system actively computes a Country Instability Index (CII) for 31 Tier-1 nations by cross-correlating escalation signals across multiple streams. Built as a native desktop application using Tauri 2 and shipping as six specialized web variants, it tracks global infrastructure, finance radars, and commodity markets seamlessly.
keyFeatures: Local AI synthesis: Synthesizes massive streams of news feeds into concise briefs entirely locally using Ollama to ensure data privacy.
Dual 3D map engines: Visualizes complex geographical data utilizing a combination of globe.gl for planetary views and deck.gl for layered flat maps.
Country Instability Index: Calculates authoritative, server-driven stress scores for global nations by correlating military and economic crisis signals.
Cross-stream correlation radar: Merges financial, military, and infrastructure data into a cohesive, seven-signal market composite radar.
Native Tauri 2 desktop app: Ships as a highly optimized, cross-platform native application for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

readmeHtml:
World Monitor

简体中文 | 日本語 | Русский

Real-time global intelligence dashboard — AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface.

The World Monitor name and wordmark identify the official site at www.worldmonitor.app, so please don't present a fork as the official site.

         

       

     

Documentation  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

Ways to Use It

Surface Get it Docs
Web app worldmonitor.app and the tech, finance, commodity, happy and energy variants Getting Started
Desktop app (Tauri) Windows, macOS and Linux downloads above Desktop App
Terminal dashboard npx worldmonitor Terminal Dashboard
CLI npm install -g worldmonitor or brew install worldmonitor Command-Line Client
SDKs Python worldmonitor-sdk, Ruby worldmonitor, Go sdk/go SDKs
MCP server https://worldmonitor.app/mcp MCP Overview

The terminal dashboard runs the same live data in your shell: world map, news, markets, conflict, military flights, cyber, climate, prediction markets and live TV, with mouse support and colour themes. No API key needed.

What It Does

  • Curated news feeds across global and regional categories, AI-synthesized into briefs
  • Dual map engine — 3D globe (globe.gl) and WebGL flat map (deck.gl) with a shared map-layer catalog
  • Panel inventory — concrete panel implementations across specialized variants
  • Cross-stream correlation — military, economic, disaster, and escalation signal convergence
  • Country Instability Index (CII) — live CII v14 scores, bands, and approximate 24-hour movement for 31 Tier-1 countries
  • Finance radar — stock exchanges, commodities, crypto, and a market composite
  • Local AI — run everything with Ollama, no API keys required
  • Site variants from a single codebase (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy)
  • Native desktop app (Tauri 2) for macOS, Windows, and Linux
  • Multilingual UI with native-language feeds and RTL support

For the full feature list, architecture, data sources, and algorithms, see the documentation.

Support Status

All site variants and desktop binaries are built from a single codebase and ship from the same release process. The table below clarifies maintenance status so you know which surfaces are safe to depend on.

Surface Status Notes
worldmonitor.app, tech., finance., commodity., happy., energy. Stable Public deployments built from this repo, actively maintained
Desktop binaries (Windows / macOS Apple Silicon / macOS Intel / Linux AppImage x64 and ARM64) Stable One Tauri binary for every variant — install World Monitor and switch to tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy in-app. There is deliberately no per-variant download
worldmonitor npm package (terminal dashboard and CLI) Stable Published from cli/ on every cli-v* tag

Issues filed against any of the above are triaged from the same backlog — see the issues board for currently-open work.

Quick Start

One-line install (self-host the full stack with Docker — dashboard, Redis, AIS relay, seeded public data):

curl -fsSL https://www.worldmonitor.app/install.sh | bash

This clones into ./worldmonitor (or reuses your checkout), generates the required secrets, starts the stack, and seeds data. Then open localhost:3000. Options: --dir, --port, --no-seed, --no-build, passed after bash -s -- (see scripts/install.sh --help). API keys are optional. Details, production notes, and uninstall: SELF_HOSTING.md.

Local development (hot-reload Vite server):

Requires Node.js 24, the version pinned in .nvmrc. Distribution packages are often older. Debian 12 and Raspberry Pi OS ship Node.js 18 with npm 9.2.0, where npm install stops with Invalid comparator: file:vendor/braces. Install Node.js 24 with nvm (nvm install inside the checkout reads .nvmrc) or from nodejs.org.

git clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git
cd worldmonitor
npm install
npm run dev

Open localhost:3000 (override the port with DEV_PORT in .env.local). The app runs with no environment variables.

Feature-specific data sources may require credentials. See .env.example for the full list.

For variant-specific development:

npm run dev:tech       # tech.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:finance    # finance.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:commodity  # commodity.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:happy      # happy.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:energy     # energy.worldmonitor.app

See the self-hosting guide for deployment options (Vercel, Docker, static).

Tech Stack

Category Technologies
Frontend Vanilla TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL
Desktop Tauri 2 (Rust) with Node.js sidecar
AI/ML Ollama / OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side)
API Contracts Protocol Buffers and sebuf HTTP annotations
Deployment Vercel Edge Functions, Railway relay, Tauri, PWA
Caching Redis (Upstash), 3-tier cache, CDN, service worker

Full stack details in the architecture docs.

Programmatic Access

World Monitor is built for agents and scripts as well as browsers:

  • MCP server — https://worldmonitor.app/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Public tools/list; tools/call authenticates with a X-WorldMonitor-Key header or OAuth. The server also publishes its Agent Skills through the draft io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension (skills/list, skills/get, and skill://… resource reads).

  • Google Antigravity and Gemini listing preparation — install the bundled Antigravity plugin (.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json + mcp_config.json) with agy plugin install ./worldmonitor. Gemini custom apps and Connected Apps sign in through Google's OAuth callbacks. See Gemini and Antigravity.

  • REST API — base https://api.worldmonitor.app, described by the OpenAPI spec.

  • CLI — the official worldmonitor npm package (source in cli/). Run it with no arguments in a terminal for the terminal dashboard:

    npx worldmonitor tools          # run ad-hoc — list every MCP tool (no key needed)
npm install -g worldmonitor     # or install the `worldmonitor` (alias `wm`) command
brew install worldmonitor       # or install it with Homebrew
worldmonitor risk IR --api-key wm_xxx

  • SDKs — official zero-dependency client libraries mirroring the CLI: Python worldmonitor-sdk (source in sdk/python/), Ruby worldmonitor (sdk/ruby/), Go github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go (sdk/go/). Guide: worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks.

Agent discovery files: llms.txt · agent-skills manifest · api-catalog. Get an API key at worldmonitor.app/pro.

Flight Data

Flight data provided graciously by Wingbits, the most advanced ADS-B flight data solution.

Supported By

World Monitor's web app and API run on Vercel. Thank you to Vercel for their generous support of the project.

Data Sources

WorldMonitor aggregates attributed upstream sources across geopolitics, finance, energy, climate, aviation, cyber, military, infrastructure, and news intelligence. Curated feeds and freshness-tracked source groups are published in the full data sources catalog, with provider, feed-tier, license-posture, and collection-method details.

Contributing

Contributions welcome! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

npm run typecheck        # Type checking
npm run build:full       # Production build

License

AGPL-3.0-only for the source code. Commercial use is permitted under the AGPL when you comply with its copyleft and source-availability terms.

Use Case Allowed?
Personal / research / educational Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only
Self-hosted instance Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only
Fork and modify Yes, share source under AGPL-3.0-only when required
Commercial use / SaaS Yes, under AGPL-3.0-only when you comply with AGPL obligations
Private-source proprietary use or official branding rights Separate commercial or trademark permission needed

See LICENSE for the full code license and docs/license.mdx for a plain-language summary. Commercial licensing is available as an alternative option for teams that need non-AGPL terms.

Copyright (C) 2026 Elie Habib. All rights reserved.

Author

Elie Habib — GitHub

Contributors

Security Acknowledgments

We thank the following researchers for responsibly disclosing security issues:

  • Cody Richard — Disclosed three security findings covering IPC command exposure, renderer-to-sidecar trust boundary analysis, and fetch patch credential injection architecture (2026)

See our Security Policy for responsible disclosure guidelines.
